analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. docs/architecture/inference.md has a date bump and a new troubleshooting row at head line ~3552, plus the supplied excerpts of the Qwen tensor-parallel sections. docs/architecture/security/provider-trust.md has a date bump and a new paragraph at head lines 128-137. No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization logic, or cache storage logic is modified, so none of the threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041, T-053, T-054, T-057) is touched in behavior.

The new provider-trust.md paragraph says a crash from missing weakly imported Date `>=` and `<=` operators on pre-release macOS 27.2 leaves App Attest pending and relaxes no authorization. That is consistent with TB-011/T-057: a crash loop causes denial of service and does not grant authorization. It also describes the stated mitigation of switching to `timeIntervalSince(_:)` with the same thresholds, and a release-build check, `scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py`. I could not verify those code changes or the script because they are not in the supplied evidence. A possible availability gap, a provider crash loop on affected macOS builds, is already documented as pending and fail-closed. It is not a regression.

The inference.md excerpts for Qwen TP batch, wavefront, native context, media ingress and the assistant describe existing mechanisms. They include per-request charge and 503 refusal, media prefix reuse disabled, and a load agreement binding wire versions. I saw no new claim that weakens the prefix-cache posture in T-041. The media ingress text says prefix reuse is disabled for that path. Integration questions for later passes: whether the code actually uses `timeIntervalSince` in the App Attest checks, and whether the weak-import check script exists and is enforced. Neither can be confirmed from this docs-only batch.
